sections.title: Grade 6 skills
sections.description: The most important words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 6.

sections.title: Grade 5 skills
sections.description: Key words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 5.

questions.question: Which word best describes something that works well while wasting as little time or energy as possible?
questions.options: wasteful | efficient | reluctant | fragile
questions.correctAnswer: efficient
questions.explanation: Something efficient does its job without wasting time, energy or effort — like a heart that pumps more blood with every beat.

questions.question: Which word means 'not enough; very small in amount'?
questions.options: meagre | substantial | extensive | massive
questions.correctAnswer: meagre
questions.explanation: A meagre amount is far too small — the opposite of substantial or extensive.

questions.question: Which word names a special right or advantage that only some people have?
questions.options: privilege | agency | observation | legacy
questions.correctAnswer: privilege
questions.explanation: A privilege is a special right or advantage — not everyone gets to enjoy it.

questions.question: Which word means 'something passed down from the past, such as a tradition or a set of values'?
questions.options: rehearsal | apprentice | legacy | advert
questions.correctAnswer: legacy
questions.explanation: A legacy is something handed down from earlier generations, like a story, a skill or a set of values.

questions.question: Which word names a young person who learns a trade or skill by working beside an experienced worker?
questions.options: admiral | apprentice | dynasty | monarch
questions.correctAnswer: apprentice
questions.explanation: An apprentice learns a trade or skill through hands-on practice beside someone experienced.

questions.question: According to 'Training Champions: The Science Behind Sport', why do trained athletes often have lower resting heart rates than people who never exercise?
questions.options: Because their hearts pump more blood with every beat, so the heart does not have to work as hard at rest. | Because they eat less food than other people. | Because they sleep for fewer hours each night. | Because their muscles stop needing oxygen.
questions.correctAnswer: Because their hearts pump more blood with every beat, so the heart does not have to work as hard at rest.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that a trained heart becomes stronger and more efficient, pumping more blood with each beat.

questions.question: In 'Reading Closely: Fact and Opinion in Health Writing', which kind of statement often uses words like 'best', 'worst' or 'should'?
questions.options: A fact | An opinion | A question | An instruction
questions.correctAnswer: An opinion
questions.explanation: The passage explains that words like 'best', 'worst', 'should' or 'I think' are clues that a statement is an opinion, not a fact.

questions.question: In 'When the Leaves Stop Speaking, part 1', what was Doctor Alina's team studying in the forest?
questions.options: Transpiration in old forests | The village's farming methods | The history of the fig tree | New building materials
questions.correctAnswer: Transpiration in old forests
questions.explanation: Doctor Alina tells Amal that her team of scientists is studying transpiration, how the forest releases water, in old forests.

questions.question: In part 2 of the story, what did some village elders believe the outsider scientists were doing?
questions.options: Spreading propaganda to seize control of the forest | Teaching children new songs | Building a new school | Selling fruit at the market
questions.correctAnswer: Spreading propaganda to seize control of the forest
questions.explanation: One elder accuses the outsiders of spreading propaganda so that they could seize control of the forest.

questions.question: At the end of part 3, what does Amal say the forest's recovery begins with?
questions.options: Belief, and the choice to act | New machinery | A change in the weather | A larger research budget
questions.correctAnswer: Belief, and the choice to act
questions.explanation: Amal says that whether you call it an old story or biology, recovery begins with belief and with the choice to act.

questions.question: Which sentence means the same as 'If you do not save a little each week, you will not reach your goal'?
questions.options: Unless you save a little each week, you will not reach your goal. | Unless you save a little each week, you will reach your goal. | If you save a little each week, you will not reach your goal. | You will reach your goal unless you do not save.
questions.correctAnswer: Unless you save a little each week, you will not reach your goal.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not', so it replaces 'if you do not' without needing a second negative.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative adverb: She finished the race ___ than everyone else in her team.
questions.options: fast | faster | fastest | more fast
questions.correctAnswer: faster
questions.explanation: Short adverbs like 'fast' form the comparative by adding -er: faster, not 'more fast'.

questions.question: Amal said, 'I am saving my money.' Which sentence reports her words correctly?
questions.options: Amal said that she is saving her money. | Amal said that she was saving her money. | Amal told that she was saving her money. | Amal said that she save her money.
questions.correctAnswer: Amal said that she was saving her money.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'I' becomes 'she' and 'am saving' moves back one step to 'was saving'.

questions.question: Which sentence is written in the past simple passive?
questions.options: The studio filmed the documentary last year. | The documentary was filmed by the studio last year. | The studio was filming the documentary last year. | The documentary films the studio last year.
questions.correctAnswer: The documentary was filmed by the studio last year.
questions.explanation: The passive puts the documentary first and uses 'was' plus the past participle 'filmed'.

questions.question: Choose the correct participle adjective: The comedy show left the whole audience ___.
questions.options: amusing | amuse | amused | amusement
questions.correctAnswer: amused
questions.explanation: The audience feels the emotion, so the -ed form is correct: the show is amusing, but the audience is amused.

questions.question: A strong opinion essay states a clear opinion and then supports it with ___.
questions.options: only personal feelings | evidence and reasons | a list of favourite things | a made-up story
questions.correctAnswer: evidence and reasons
questions.explanation: An opinion essay is more convincing when the writer backs up their view with reasons and evidence, not feelings alone.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a rhetorical question to persuade the reader?
questions.options: Pocket money should be saved, not spent all at once. | Isn't it wiser to save a little each week than to spend it all at once? | I received pocket money last Saturday. | Some children receive pocket money weekly.
questions.correctAnswer: Isn't it wiser to save a little each week than to spend it all at once?
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question invites the reader to agree without expecting a spoken answer — a common persuasive-writing technique.

questions.question: Which connecting word best links two ideas that contrast with each other across paragraphs?
questions.options: however | firstly | in addition | finally
questions.correctAnswer: however
questions.explanation: 'However' signals a contrast between the idea before it and the idea after it, unlike 'firstly' or 'in addition', which add ideas rather than contrast them.

questions.question: Which sentence is written in the more formal register suitable for a public report?
questions.options: That broken swing needs fixing ASAP, it's driving everyone mad! | The council should repair the broken swing without delay. | Fix the swing already, come on! | Ugh, that swing has been broken forever.
questions.correctAnswer: The council should repair the broken swing without delay.
questions.explanation: A public report uses formal, measured language, avoiding slang and exclamation marks.

questions.question: A balanced argument about screen time should ___.
questions.options: only give one side of the issue | present both sides fairly before reaching a conclusion | avoid stating any opinion at all | copy somebody else's opinion
questions.correctAnswer: present both sides fairly before reaching a conclusion
questions.explanation: A balanced argument weighs both sides fairly before the writer reaches and explains their own conclusion.

questions.question: Which word names the good things in food and drink that help a body grow and stay well?
questions.options: nutrition | survival | residence | ancestor
questions.correctAnswer: nutrition
questions.explanation: Nutrition is the nourishment food gives the body so it can grow and stay healthy.

questions.question: Which word describes something made by people rather than grown or formed in nature?
questions.options: artificial | native | marine | continental
questions.correctAnswer: artificial
questions.explanation: Something artificial is made by people, unlike something natural, which grows or forms on its own.

questions.question: Which word describes someone who does not want to do something or feels unsure about it?
questions.options: eager | reluctant | grateful | dutiful
questions.correctAnswer: reluctant
questions.explanation: Someone reluctant hesitates or holds back because they are unwilling or unsure.

questions.question: Which word describes something that brings a huge change, completely new and different from before?
questions.options: colonial | historical | revolutionary | cultural
questions.correctAnswer: revolutionary
questions.explanation: Something revolutionary causes a dramatic, sweeping change rather than a small adjustment.

questions.question: In 'The Camel and the Sparrow', why could Zara find the hidden stream when nobody on the ground could?
questions.options: She flew higher than any camel could reach, so she saw what nobody on the ground could see. | She had a map that showed the stream's location. | The village elder told her exactly where to look. | She followed the camel's footprints in the sand.
questions.correctAnswer: She flew higher than any camel could reach, so she saw what nobody on the ground could see.
questions.explanation: The fable says that from up in the sky, Zara saw a thin green line that nobody on the ground could spot.

questions.question: In 'The Silence After the Rumble, part 1', what were Amal's two jobs at the courthouse each morning?
questions.options: Sweeping the steps and filling the water jug on the judge's bench. | Guarding the doors and collecting the mail. | Cooking breakfast and cleaning the windows. | Selling tickets and greeting visitors.
questions.correctAnswer: Sweeping the steps and filling the water jug on the judge's bench.
questions.explanation: The passage says her role was simple: sweep the steps and fill the water jug on the judge's bench.

questions.question: In 'The Legend of the Whispering Dunes', why does Zara refuse to run towards the pool of blue water her cousin points at?
questions.options: She recognises it as a mirage and knows the true spring is the one that whispers. | She is too tired to run any further. | Her grandmother forbids her from drinking unfamiliar water. | She cannot see the pool clearly enough.
questions.correctAnswer: She recognises it as a mirage and knows the true spring is the one that whispers.
questions.explanation: Zara tells her cousin that the blue pool is a mirage, a trick of the light, and that the real spring is the one that hums.

questions.question: Omar and Amal both describe the same market morning, but Amal mentions the spice seller's dried hibiscus petals and Omar does not. Why might that be?
questions.options: Omar was busy selling fish at his own stall, so he never saw the gift at the next stall. | Omar does not like hibiscus petals. | Amal invented the detail to make her account more exciting. | The spice seller only spoke to Amal, not to any adults.
questions.correctAnswer: Omar was busy selling fish at his own stall, so he never saw the gift at the next stall.
questions.explanation: A narrator can only report what they notice, so each account keeps the details that mattered most to that person.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly completes the adjective-plus-preposition pair?
questions.options: She was proud of her team's victory. | She was proud for her team's victory. | She was proud her team's victory. | She was proud on her team's victory.
questions.correctAnswer: She was proud of her team's victory.
questions.explanation: 'Proud' is always followed by 'of' — dropping the preposition or choosing the wrong one breaks the sentence.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a defining relative clause?
questions.options: The explorer who made the discovery shared it with her team. | The explorer, who made the discovery, shared it with her team. | The explorer which made the discovery shared it with her team. | The explorer whom made the discovery shared it with her team.
questions.correctAnswer: The explorer who made the discovery shared it with her team.
questions.explanation: A defining relative clause about a person uses 'who' with no commas, because the clause is essential to knowing which explorer is meant.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the comparative correctly?
questions.options: Route B was hotter and riskier than Route A. | Route B was more hotter and more riskier than Route A. | Route B was hottest and riskiest than Route A. | Route B was hotter and riskier as Route A.
questions.correctAnswer: Route B was hotter and riskier than Route A.
questions.explanation: Short adjectives take the -er ending alone; adding 'more' as well creates a double comparative, which is incorrect.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses an opinion phrase?
questions.options: In my opinion, the mural should be preserved. | In my opinion that the mural should be preserved. | In my opinion the mural should be preserved that. | In my opinion of the mural should be preserved.
questions.correctAnswer: In my opinion, the mural should be preserved.
questions.explanation: 'In my opinion' is followed by a comma and then the clause — never by the word 'that'.

questions.question: A fable is deliberately kept short and focused on one problem so that ___.
questions.options: readers can finish it quickly before school | nothing distracts from the lesson at the end | it can be performed as a play | it fits on a single page
questions.correctAnswer: nothing distracts from the lesson at the end
questions.explanation: A fable tells one problem quickly so the moral at the end stands out clearly, unlike a novel with room for many characters and years.

questions.question: Which detail signals that a tale is a legend rather than a myth?
questions.options: It explains a natural event, like why the sea is salty. | It grows out of a real place, a real period of history, or a person who may once have lived. | It always features talking animals. | It never has an ending.
questions.correctAnswer: It grows out of a real place, a real period of history, or a person who may once have lived.
questions.explanation: A legend is rooted in something real before storytellers add unlikely details, while a myth explains a natural event and features gods or spirits.

questions.question: A three-sentence synopsis of a story should ___.
questions.options: describe every character in full detail | sum up only the most important events in a few sentences | quote the story word for word | focus only on the setting
questions.correctAnswer: sum up only the most important events in a few sentences
questions.explanation: A synopsis is a short summary that captures the main events, not every detail from the full story.

questions.question: When retelling the same event from a different character's point of view, a writer should ___.
questions.options: copy the first account word for word | include only the details that character would actually notice or care about | invent a completely different event | ignore what happened and describe something else instead
questions.correctAnswer: include only the details that character would actually notice or care about
questions.explanation: Like Omar and Amal's two accounts of the same market morning, each narrator notices different details, so a good retelling stays true to that character's viewpoint.
